Japanese listed company Remixpoint clears out ETH, SOL, XRP, DOGE—leaves only 1,506 BTC

Japanese listed company Remixpoint has liquidated all altcoins and fully shifted to a single-coin BTC strategy.

Remixpoint is a company listed in Tokyo. Previously, its holdings were quite diversified: it held ETH, SOL, XRP, and DOGE. Now it has sold everything, leaving only about 1,506 BTC, worth roughly $115 million. In plain terms, it cuts off all altcoins and bets on a single asset. This approach is similar to MicroStrategy’s route—public-company treasuries are increasingly leaning toward “trusting only BTC.”

Impact on the market
- Short term: Mostly bearish sentiment. When a listed company leads with clearing out ETH, SOL, and XRP, it sends an institutional signal: the treasury allocation value of altcoins is being downgraded. Current prices: ETH at $2,380.69 (24h -3.25%), SOL at $98.13 (-4.12%), XRP at $1.324 (-4.33%). They were already falling, so this news adds more pressure. BTC was not spared either, at $76,692.89 (-1.85%).
- Medium term: If more companies’ treasuries follow a “BTC only” approach, the institutional-demand narrative for altcoins will weaken further, and capital stratification will become even more extreme.

One-sentence translation: Institutions aren’t leaving crypto—they’re leaving “everything except BTC.”

My take
This isn’t bearish for BTC itself, but it is a real hit to confidence in ETH and altcoins. ETH is down more than BTC today (-3.25% vs -1.85%). If more companies follow by clearing out, the ETH/BTC ratio will likely continue to weaken. For BTC, I’m more of a wait-and-see stance: if the $76,692.89 level can’t hold, bearish sentiment below may amplify; if it stabilizes, this news will likely be digested into a neutral-to-bullish narrative about institutions focusing on BTC. Don’t rush to treat short-term altcoin rebounds as a reversal—the risk is on the institutional side, not on the retail side.

日本上市企业Remixpoint清仓所有山寨币，全面转向BTC单币策略。

Remixpoint是家在东京上市的公司，之前持仓挺分散：ETH、SOL、XRP、DOGE都有。现在全卖了，只剩大约1506枚BTC，价值1.15亿美元左右。说白了就是把山寨全砍掉，押注单一资产。这种做法跟MicroStrategy路线趋同——上市公司财库配置越来越倾向“只信BTC”。

对市场的影响
- 短期：利空情绪为主。上市公司带头清仓ETH、SOL、XRP，等于给机构圈递了个信号：山寨币的财库配置价值在被降级。当前ETH报$2,380.69（24h -3.25%）、SOL $98.13（-4.12%）、XRP $1.324（-4.33%），本身就在跌，这个消息是雪上加霜。BTC也没躲开，$76,692.89（-1.85%）。
- 中期：如果更多企业财库跟进“BTC only”，山寨币的机构需求叙事会进一步弱化，资金分层会更极端。

一句话翻译：机构不是在离开crypto，是在离开“除了BTC以外的一切”。

这事对BTC本身算不上利空，但对ETH和山寨是实打实的信心打击。ETH今天跌得比BTC狠（-3.25% vs -1.85%），如果后续再有公司跟进清仓，ETH/BTC比价大概率继续走弱。BTC这边我偏观望：$76,692.89这个位置如果守不住，下方看跌情绪会放大；能企稳则这个消息会被消化成“机构聚焦BTC”的中性偏多叙事。山寨短期反弹别急着当反转，风险在机构端不在散户端。

Texas grid can’t take it anymore: new data center connections are halted—has the era of AI mining for power come to an end?

Texas has paused new data center grid interconnections, interrupting power-supply expectations for AI expansion and Bitcoin mining.

ERCOT, the Texas power grid operator, has suspended approval of new data center grid-connection applications due to pressure on electricity demand. In recent years, Texas has been a hot spot for AI data centers and Bitcoin mining farms—cheap electricity, lax regulation, and compute capacity across the U.S. has been clustering there. Now the grid has effectively said, “Don’t come yet,” indicating demand has already hit the infrastructure’s ceiling. For miners, getting stuck at the site-approval stage means expansion plans are put on hold, and early investments could end up wasted.

One-sentence translation: It’s not that we don’t want AI—it’s that there isn’t enough electricity yet. First come, first served—those who arrive later wait in line.

Impact on the market
- Short term: sentiment is bearish. BTC is now $77,539.5, down 1.15% over 24 hours; ETH is $2,417.41, down 1.90%. With the market already weak, adding “mining-related bearish news” will likely intensify risk-off sentiment.
- Medium term: if other states follow with power curbs, miners’ costs will rise and compute growth will slow. The industry logic will shift from “unlimited expansion” to “competing for limited existing power resources.” States with excess power and miners with their own power plants may benefit instead.

My take
This news alone won’t collapse the broader market—BTC’s core drivers are still liquidity and macro factors. However, it is a signal of an energy bottleneck. Sooner or later, both the AI narrative and the mining narrative will have to face the hard constraint of electricity prices. In the short term, I’m cautious: if BTC breaks below the support around $100.39K, sentiment will worsen further; if it holds, this turns into consolidation. Mostly watch and wait, and see which direction the market chooses on its own.

德州暂停新数据中心接入电网，AI扩张和比特币挖矿的电力供给预期被打断。

德州电网运营商（ERCOT）因为电力需求压力，暂停批准新的数据中心并网申请。德州这几年是AI数据中心和比特币矿场的热土，电便宜、监管松，全美的算力都在往那儿挤。现在电网直接说“先别来了”，说明需求已经顶到基础设施上限。对矿企来说，新场地审批卡住等于扩张计划搁置，前期投入可能打水漂。

这个消息本身打不崩大盘，BTC的核心驱动还是流动性和宏观。但它是能源瓶颈的一个信号，AI叙事和挖矿叙事迟早都要面对电价这个硬约束。短期我偏谨慎，BTC若失守$100.39K一线支撑，情绪会进一步转差；守住的话就是震荡消化。观望为主，等方向自己走出来。

The SEC has taken a critical step in preparations for 24/7 trading on US stock markets.

The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has announced the agenda and panelists for a roundtable meeting to be held on September 17, 2026.

What Will Be Discussed at the Meeting?

The meeting, to be held at SEC headquarters, will focus on extending trading hours on US stock markets. In this context, preparations for US stock markets to trade during nighttime hours, i.e., 24/7, will be prioritized. The meeting will evaluate the current preparations of exchanges, brokerage firms, and other market organizations.

A System Similar to Cryptocurrency Markets is on the Agenda!

 The SEC aims to pave the way for traditional stock markets to trade for longer hours, similar to cryptocurrency markets. The technical and operational aspects of a model allowing investors to buy and sell stocks at any time of day, as in cryptocurrency markets, will be evaluated.

The meeting will specifically address how night trading can be conducted, market surveillance, liquidity, clearing and settlement processes, and investor protection.

Major Financial Institutions to Attend!

The SEC has managed to bring together some of Wall Street's largest institutions at this meeting.

The announcement stated that representatives from 17 major firms will attend. These include giants such as BlackRock, Citi, Nasdaq, NYSE, Cboe, FINRA, State Street, Citadel Securities, UBS, Robinhood, and Charles Schwab.

Strive’s new tool, SATA, raised funds over ten days to buy 143 BTC, adding another player to the corporate holdings track.

In plain terms, SATA—an Asset Management product from Strive—is a structured product that bundles high-yield notes with BTC exposure. Over the past 10 days, it has been continuously raising capital and has already reached the amount needed to buy 143 BTC. At the current price of $77,432, that’s roughly an $11 million order of magnitude. While the absolute figure isn’t huge, the pace has been steady—10 consecutive days, buying every day, a slow-and-steady accumulation.

One-sentence translation: It’s not a one-time, appropriately sized allocation—it’s turning retail investors’ money into a BTC-buying pipeline that runs every day.

Market impact
- Short term: $11 million is barely a drop in the bucket compared with BTC’s daily trading volume, so it has limited impact on price. But continuous accumulation itself is a “buy-side” narrative that keeps sentiment somewhat warm. BTC is currently trading sideways around $77,432; this kind of ongoing marginal buying is healthier than one-off large orders.
- Medium term: What’s really worth watching is whether the model can be replicated. If a “high yield + BTC” structure like SATA works, it could give other asset managers a ready-made route. Corporate-grade holding tools would expand from MSTR’s single path of “issuing debt to buy coins” into a diversified product lineup. That matters far more than any one headline.

Bullish on the direction. 143 BTC is just the beginning—the key is whether this model can keep raising funds and whether it can be copied. As long as BTC holds the $77,000 area, the marginal buying keeps stacking up, and the medium-term supply contraction logic stays intact. The risk is where the high yield in the structured product comes from—if it relies on volatility or derivatives returns, it could backfire in a bear market. That’s something to monitor regarding SATA’s fund-raising sustainability.

【Trading volume is expanding, but prices are still grinding—do you understand this signal?】

This week, ETH has been moving in a rather tangled way. Over the past 24 hours, it’s down 1.2%, and over 7 days, it’s down 3.3%. It doesn’t look like a heavy drop, but it’s that kind of dull blade cutting feeling that’s the most frustrating. Key support at 2310 hasn’t been broken, and key resistance at 2474 can’t be pushed through either—so it’s just stuck there.

What’s interesting is the trading volume.

While price drifts downward, volume has been staying high. What does that mean? Both bulls and bears are pushing chips into the market, but neither side has been able to knock the other out decisively. Technically, we call this “building a position,” but I’d rather say—large capital is rebalancing and rotating.

Arthur Hayes said this week that ETH is his first choice and even called out the “potential for 3 to 5x.” On the same day, however, Japanese company Remixpoint sold off nearly all of the ETH, SOL, and XRP it held, leaving only BTC as the lone survivor.

See—when it comes to the market, some people spot an opportunity to enter, while others think uncertainty is reason enough to retreat. That’s the real market: not one solid block of consensus, but everyone acting based on their own judgment.

So how should we look at next week?

Honestly, I haven’t changed my stance. At ETH’s current level—more than a 50% pullback from its ATH—historically this range is often a value zone where long-term capital starts building. The problem is, the market currently lacks a catalyst that’s decisive enough to trigger everything. ETF approvals, the RWA narrative, staking yields—these logics are still there, but in the short term, they just can’t get the momentum going.

I’ve been thinking about one thing lately: does ETH’s “business logic” really hold up?

DeFi is still there, staking annualized yields of 5%-7% are still running, and the RWA story is gradually coming to life. But the issue is that when BTC’s spotlight is too bright, money naturally gravitates toward it. ETH isn’t necessarily bad—it just needs a stronger catalyst to pull people over from BTC.

So my view is this: direction is approaching the moment of choice, and volume will speak. If next week breaks above 2474 with volume, then the short-term trade could be worth considering; if it’s still just grinding, then we’ll keep waiting. Don’t chase pumps, don’t trade against the trend—just follow the market.

Has your view this week changed?

To be honest, I didn’t move on short-term execution. But after seeing Hayes and Remixpoint take two completely opposite approaches, I’m even more convinced of one thing: disagreement in the market is itself an opportunity— the bigger the divergence, the more violent the move when the direction finally gets selected.

Do you think ETH can break 2474 this time, or will it come with another round of cleansing?

【成交量在放大，但价格还在磨——这个信号你看懂了吗？】

这周ETH走得很拧巴。24小时-1.2%，7天-3.3%，看着跌不多，但那种钝刀子割肉的感觉最磨人。关键支撑2310还没破，关键阻力2474也上不去，就这么僵着。

有意思的是成交量。

价格阴跌，成交量却一直维持在高位。这说明什么？多空双方都在往里怼筹码，但谁也没本事把对方彻底打趴下。技术上管这叫"蓄势"，但我更愿意说——大资金在调仓换手。

Arthur Hayes这周说ETH是他第一选择，喊出"3到5倍"的潜力。同一天，日本公司Remixpoint却把手里ETH、SOL、XRP清得差不多，只留了BTC这一个独苗。

你看，同样看市场，有人看到机会在入场，有人觉得不确定在撤退。这才是真实的市场——不是铁板一块，而是每个人按自己的判断在行动。

那下周怎么看？

说实话，我没改变立场。ETH现在这个位置，从ATH回撤超过50%，历史上这种区间往往是长线资金开始建仓的价值区域。但问题是，现在市场没有那种一锤定音的催化剂。ETF审批、RWA叙事、质押收益——这些逻辑都还在，但短期就是带不动。

我最近在想一件事：ETH的"商业逻辑"到底成不成立？

DeFi还在，质押年化5%-7%跑得动，RWA叙事慢慢在落地。但问题是，当BTC的光环太亮的时候，资金就是会往那边聚。ETH不是不好，是需要更强的催化剂才能把人从BTC那边拽过来。

所以我的判断是：方向选择在即，成交量会说话。如果下周往上突破2474且带量，那短线可以做一做；如果还是磨，那就继续等。别追涨，别逆势，顺着市场走。

这周你的看法有没有变过？

说实话，短期操作上我没动。但看了Hayes和Remixpoint这两个完全相反的操作，我反而更确认了一件事：市场的分歧本身就是机会——分歧越大，方向选出来的时候，行情越猛。

你觉得ETH这次能突破2474吗？还是说会再来一波清洗？

How many typical traits do guys in the crypto world have? They’re calculating, highly prone to gambling, love arbitrage, and if they can get something for free they’ll never pay.

And honestly, there’s no way around it. The crypto world might be one of the markets with the richest variety of global financial derivatives and the most arbitrage opportunities. Someone who initially didn’t understand finance at all can, after a few years of struggling and learning in crypto, go through futures, options, leverage, liquidations, hedging—then play through another round of DeFi. Their real-world experience in financial games may not be any worse than that of a finance PhD.

Especially after DeFi came along, borrowing, loop lending, LPs, hedging, arbitrage—every kind of financial structure is practiced day after day using real money.

So if you really try to treat crypto guys as “prey,” it’s actually the hardest group to catch.

You think you’re calculating their money—but they may have been calculating your odds, your costs, and your exit path since day one.

Even if you truly do manage to make a haul in the beginning, you’re still very likely to end up getting reverse-arbitraged in the end.

So going after a woman to catch a crypto guy is often the least cost-effective business.

You think you’re setting up the scheme, but from the moment they meet you, they may have already worked out the risk-reward ratio.

What the crypto world lacks the least is people who, after seeing bubbles, scams, and blow-off rallies followed by crashes, can still stay calm and unflinching.

title: Esquemas Piramidales y ponzi
subTitle:
La mayoría de las personas que invierten en Bitcoin o en cualquier otra criptomoneda, o que deciden participar en los eventos de la Oferta Inicial de Monedas (ICO, por sus siglas en inglés), generalmente están preocupadas por dos cosas. Primero, el retorno de la inversión (ROI), que representa los beneficios que obtendrán con la inversión inicial. Luego, hay una segunda preocupación, que está relacionada con la cantidad de riesgo involucrado con la inversión. Cuando los riesgos son demasiado altos, es más probable que los inversionistas pierdan su inversión inicial (en partes o por completo), lo que resultaría en un ROI negativo.
Naturalmente, siempre hay algún grado de riesgo involucrado con cualquier inversión. Sin embargo, el riesgo aumenta considerablemente en los casos en que el inversionista se involucra inesperadamente en esquemas Ponzi o pirámide, que son ilegales. Por lo tanto, es de gran importancia poder identificar estos esquemas y comprender cómo funcionan.
#BTC #BNB #ETH #Ponzi #piramidal

First, the return on investment (ROI), which represents the benefits they will obtain from the initial investment. Then, there is a second concern, which is related to the amount of risk involved with the investment. When risks are too high, it is more likely that investors will lose their initial investment (in part or entirely), resulting in a negative ROI.

Circle’s CEO has publicly urged the US: if you want the US dollar’s hegemony to continue, rely on stablecoins—don’t wait for other countries to move first.

Circle is the issuer of USDC. It holds hundreds of billions of dollars worth of stablecoins. This time, their CEO went straight to Washington: in the arena of digital finance, the US must be the boss. The logic is simple—global payment systems are migrating from SWIFT’s legacy architecture to the on-chain world. Whoever controls the entry point for digital dollars controls the next-generation global settlement network. In essence, stablecoins are on-chain proxies for the US dollar. Every USDC unit that circulates overseas extends US dollar influence.

- Short term: sentiment is slightly warming. The stablecoin narrative is reigniting. BTC is currently $77,210 (24h -0.59%), and ETH is $2,384.52 (-2.19%). Senior executives have been densely voicing their stance to regulators, which suggests Washington’s attitude toward stablecoin legislation is softening. Once the US formalizes clear rules for stablecoins, the on-chain dollar supply could take another step up—historically, when stablecoin total supply expands, the cycle is basically the same as a crypto market inflow/additional capital cycle.

SEC invites Blackrock, Nasdaq, and Citadel to a meeting: US stocks want to learn from crypto and trade 7×24

US stocks want to discuss 7×24-hour trading, and the years-long playbook from crypto has been officially recognized by TradFi.

What’s going on
This week, the SEC released a list of participants for a public roundtable discussion. The heavyweight players on Wall Street—such as Blackrock, Nasdaq, and Citadel—are all on the roster. The only topic is this: can US stocks trade 7 days a week, 24 hours a day, without interruption? Put simply, since the first BTC exchange went live more than a decade ago, crypto has been operating on 7×24×365, while US stocks are still only open for about 6.5 hours a day and closed on weekends. Now regulators are actively calling in major TradFi players to study the issue—effectively acknowledging that this model is a trend rather than an oddity.

One-line translation: crypto’s playbook is becoming the standard configuration for financial markets.

Market impact
- Short term: a positive tailwind for sentiment. Regulators proactively studying extending trading hours is a form of validation for the entire crypto narrative. In the market moves for BTC $77,160 and ETH $2,380, this kind of news will reinforce the “TradFi moving toward Crypto” narrative. But note: this is a slow-moving variable, not a catalyst that immediately brings in fresh capital. Don’t expect a surge within 12 hours.
- Medium term: if US stocks truly move toward 7×24, market-making, clearing, and custody infrastructure will be forced to upgrade. Crypto already has more than a decade of first-mover experience in this area. Blackrock—the issuer of the BTC spot ETF—is also on the attendee list. The integration of traditional and crypto infrastructure will accelerate.

My take
Bullish—more so in the medium term than in the short term. BTC’s short-term price action around $77,160 is consolidating on reduced volume. This news isn’t a hype or pump catalyst; it’s a narrative reinforcement. It changes capital’s aesthetics over the next 6 to 12 months, not tonight’s candlesticks. The risk is that this roundtable is only a discussion with no timeline—don’t treat it as already-implemented good news. BTC apparent demand turns negative again; the August rebound barely started and got pushed back down: who’s selling?

BTC on-chain demand indicators have flipped negative again, and price is stuck below $77,318—its rebound momentum has run out.

In on-chain analysis, there’s a metric called “apparent demand.” In simple terms, it estimates real buying pressure by working backward from newly issued BTC supply and exchange outflow data. According to CoinTelegraph, this indicator briefly improved early in August and then turned negative again. Meanwhile, BTC has fallen 0.34% over the past 24 hours and is now at $77,318. The reason is a weak broader environment—both the bond market and the stock market are being sold off together, and risk assets are getting hit.

One-sentence translation: The August rebound wasn’t “real money” coming in—just a pause after selling pressure, and now that breath has run out again.

Market impact
- Short term: The transmission is pretty direct—on-chain real buying demand shrinks → ETF and retail funds don’t step in to absorb it → BTC can only fight it out using existing liquidity, with the $77K level repeatedly getting tested. If bonds and equities both decline, institutional risk controls will cut risk-asset exposure first, and BTC will be hit hardest. ETH is following down even more sharply: -1.66% over 24 hours, and its high-beta profile at $2,391.46 is staring us in the face.
- Medium term: If the demand indicator keeps turning negative as a norm, it suggests that the logic of this cycle—“demand taking over after the halving”—is weakening. The valuation mid-point may need to drop by another step.

My view
Bearish, but I won’t chase shorts. With apparent demand turning negative again and a sell-off across major asset classes, the probability of a downward move in the short term is high. If $77K breaks, the next area to watch is the August low region. On the other hand, if the bond market stabilizes and the indicator returns to positive, this could just be a false breakdown. There are only two key things to monitor: whether $77K can hold, and when ETF flows turn positive. ETH is weaker than BTC—$2,391.46 isn’t a safe spot.
